configs.description: The unit as the photographs show it, with a DC power jack.
configs.name: default

gaps.note: The held photographs show the front and the rear only. The four other faces are sized from the product page and drawn empty.
gaps.wanted: A photograph or drawing of the sides, the top and the underside.

gaps.note: The rear photograph shows each RJ-45 jack with its latch notch at the top and its contacts at the bottom. It also shows the WAN and LAN lamps in the top corners. The shared jack parts draw the contacts at the top and the lamps at the bottom. No part is changed here.
gaps.wanted: A decision on the shared RJ-45 parts, or a second photograph of the rear.

gaps.note: The product page lists a Digi CORE plug-in LTE modem and the front prints two SIM lamps and a SIM select button on the rear. No held photograph shows an antenna connector or a SIM slot, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: A photograph or the hardware guide showing where the antennas and SIM slots are.

gaps.note: The product page lists no mounting kit for the unit and no document held shows a mounting hole.
The photographs are 800 px wide. The legends that resolve are drawn; the fine print on the rear near the power jack does not resolve and is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: A higher resolution photograph of each face.

gaps.note: The page names the lamps and no colour or state of any of them. The two lamps in each Ethernet jack are not described.
The page states an input rating and no power consumed by the unit.

gaps.wanted: an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: The product page prints "228 mm x 127 mm x 25 mm (9.0 in x 5.0 in x 1.0 in)" labelled L x W x H. Read with the photographs, 228 is the width of the faces, 127 the depth and 25 the height.

colour.note: The front and rear are off-white (244, 245, 243 read off the photographs) with dark legends and grey-green lamps. The jacks have bright metal shields.

front-layout.note: From the front photograph: the lamps on one centreline 12.5 from the top, power at 77.1, online at 86.7, backup at 96.9, LTE/3G at 162.4, the five signal lamps from 172.3 on a 5.0 pitch, and the two SIM lamps at 202.3 and 207.2. The legends sit 6.5 below the lamps, the SIM numerals above them. A thin vertical rule stands at 70.7 and another at 213.6.

front-panel.note: The front photograph shows a rounded inner panel inside the plate. It is read at the face's scale across and as a fraction of its height down. It sits 6.1 from the left and 2.4 from the top, 216.0 wide and 20.7 high, with a corner radius of about 2. It is good to about 1.5 mm. The right inset is drawn at 5.9 mm, where the photograph reads 4.5 to 5.4 mm. The panel's edge is a faint shade, so that inset is the least certain figure.

gate-1.note: The front photograph spans 713 px for the 228 mm width (3.13 px/mm) and the rear 727 px (3.19 px/mm); the two differ by 2 per cent, so each face is read at its own scale across. Down, the photographs include the top edge of the box, so every y is a fraction of the face's own height (25 mm) read off the plate's top and bottom edges. Every position is good to about 1.5 mm.

lamps.note: The product page lists "Power, online, and LTE status, (5) signal strength and (2) SIM selection". The front photograph prints PWR, ONLINE, BACKUP, LTE/3G, SIGNAL and SIM 1 and 2, so a backup lamp is drawn that the page's list does not name. Nothing states a colour or a state, so the lamps carry on and off only.

ports.note: The product page lists "(4) Serial ports RJ-45 RS-232" and "(2) RJ-45; 10/100 Mbps (auto-sensing)". The rear photograph prints WAN over the first jack, LAN over the second and "RS232 SERIAL" under the four serial jacks.

power.note: The product page prints "18 V DC, .66 A; 100-240 AC" as the power input; the rear photograph prints "18V 1.0A" under the jack. The two are stated as printed and are not reconciled: the page's figure may be the supply's output and the legend the jack's rating. The jack is the library's barrel jack, which claims no diameter. No power consumed by the unit is stated.

rear-layout.note: From the rear photograph: the power jack centred at 12.2, the erase button at 30.7, the WAN jack centred at 49.9, the LAN jack at 72.5, four serial jacks from 96.9 on a 16.3 pitch, and the SIM select button at 162.4. The jacks are on one centreline 10.6 from the top. The serial jacks sit in one metal frame. It is drawn from 88.9 to 153.6 across and 4.5 to 17.5 down. Each opening is the library's ganged RJ-45 cell, 12.7 wide. The erase and SIM select buttons are small round marks in the photograph, drawn as the library's recessed pinhole button. The page does not describe either.

sources.note: Digi Connect IT 4 product page (digi.com, read 2026-11-05): ports, lamps, power, size and weight. The Connect IT 4 front photograph and rear photograph (800 px wide each, straight on): every position, legend and colour below. No data sheet or user guide is held; the data sheet is behind a form on the maker's site and the user guide is a link to a document not held.
